subject.title: fix(logging): keep JSON console output structured across CLI routes

question: Should `logging.consoleStyle: "json"` be treated as a process-wide contract for early CLI validation, route-first diagnostics, captured native console methods, and raw subsystem output, while leaving explicit command `--json` results unwrapped?
rationale: The patch is a technically coherent repair, but it intentionally defines the boundary of an operator-facing logging contract across all CLI execution paths; the protected maintainer state indicates that acceptance requires maintainer intent.

options.title: Adopt process-wide JSONL
options.body: Merge the branch and make the explicit JSON console-style setting cover all repaired diagnostic paths while preserving raw command-result JSON.

options.title: Limit JSON wrapping
options.body: Narrow the patch to selected logging paths if maintainers want early validation or native console diagnostics to remain outside the JSONL contract.

options.title: Pause for contract design
options.body: Keep the PR open and document a narrower logging-surface policy before selecting an implementation.

recommendation.title: Adopt process-wide JSONL
recommendation.body: Merge the branch and make the explicit JSON console-style setting cover all repaired diagnostic paths while preserving raw command-result JSON.

likelyOwner.reason: Steipete owns the current consolidated implementation and is positioned to clarify or narrow the intended CLI logging boundary.
